qualification.status: Cubature 1.12.2-0.1.4.0, built for Cleanroom from a clean checkout of this commit; over 70ed8b18 it changes workspace tooling (finding Riven as a sibling checkout) and drops the MixinItemMap Mixin entry that named no class, so its JAR and sources JAR differ from that commit's only in cubicchunks.mixins.fixes.json and the evidence below stands; a native smoke start with these bytes logged no missing Mixin on server or client; 320 Cubature tests and 82 lab tests, 0 failures. Nine one-view tour joins on two fresh Riven instances with these classes (only NOTICE.md and MODIFICATIONS.md differ in the JAR) showed no Distant Horizons no-world assertion and no fatal disconnect at stop; three dropped a full-data request that arrived after DH closed its world. Native runs of fresh 8 km Riven worlds with the bytes of ca52295d, which this commit extends only by that guard (BASELINE, 8 DH workers, LOD trace, the join at Y 320 over ground at Y 77-121): lifecycle flights at 16 and 34 blocks/s and a 16 blocks/s flight with DH's lodOnlyMode passed every scenario (flight tick p95 44.8 and 46.0 ms; the coarse LOD over the join answered 0.1-2.6 s after arrival and the ground under it shown at full view). A whole 8 km world pregenerated with its DH data (33.5 GB) and fetch flights over it passed with the pregenerator of e3782418-f7320158. The lab's lost full-view teleport stays open (Cubature docs/LOD-DELIVERY.md). Server logs of those runs show only what every earlier run showed: the missing MixinItemMap (removed in this commit), duplicate furnace recipes, two unknown Biomes O' Plenty biome names and, in some runs, a connection reset as the client quits.
qualification.contents: Version 0.1.4.0 with Orthrus Research as copyright holder and vendor and compile-only build inputs that a standalone clone fetches; since the initial commit, the manual CI workflow's build-input step, deliveryMode as the only delivery input, the periodic autosave as a named provider call, explicit delivery generation timing with run-or-await for work in flight, sender-chosen PacketCubes sizing, a provider and lighting that reach the player cube map only through CubeDemand and SurfaceHeightListener, held teleports kept when a teleport leaves the player in place, PlayerCubeMap, CubeProviderServer and the lab's Python tools split into focused parts, the delivery system in its own core.server.delivery package behind a boundary test, every numeric setting ranged and checked on sync and by the set command, and every test source run on both loaders, every test source run on Cleanroom, the Java 8 Forge fallback retired, and a bounded build pool offered to the generator through ICubeGenerator.useBuildPool (generatorBuildThreads), and regional preparation ahead of the players through ICubeGenerator.prepareRegion (regionalPreparationReachBlocks) under a contention governor, held teleports kept through vanilla's corrections of a client's moves, and a held teleport that ends without completing logged with its cause, Distant Horizons previews held while the native view is behind, previews sampled on Cubature's own pool paced by the tick's tail (previewThreads), and Distant Horizons' block-state wrappers cached per preview tile, the lab's spectator flight at 4 to 40 blocks/s, a pregenerator that writes a whole world at full height with its Distant Horizons data, and Distant Horizons sections asked for in the order the player reaches them (the arrival plan: coverage first, 1-block detail recovered at rest, the 1-block ring while the server can afford it, ground the native view misses asked for with coverage), with preview tiles held only for a native view that shows its player's ground, and Distant Horizons messages left undecoded while no DH world is loaded (a dedicated server closes DH's world before it disconnects its players).
